name: The Taj Mahal Palace, Mumbai
why_special: 1903 sea-facing heritage palace facing the Gateway of India — twin-wing property (Palace 1903 + Tower 1973), 285 rooms across 11 acres, the most-photographed hotel in India. Sea Lounge afternoon-tea ritual and Harbour Bar (Mumbai's oldest licensed bar, 1933) anchor the experience.

name: The Oberoi Mumbai
why_special: Nariman Point tower with Arabian Sea views from every sea-facing room and the Queen's Necklace Marine Drive sweep below. 287 rooms, Ziya (Vineet Bhatia's Michelin-starred Indian) on the lobby level, calmer counterpoint to the Taj's Gateway bustle.

name: Trident Nariman Point
why_special: Sister-property to The Oberoi in the same Nariman Point seafront complex — same Arabian Sea views at roughly 40% less than the Oberoi tower. India Jones (pan-Asian) and Frangipani run the dining. Best value sea-view 5-star in South Mumbai.

name: Four Seasons Hotel Mumbai
why_special: 33-floor glass tower in Worli with Aer rooftop bar on level 34 — Mumbai's most-photographed skyline view. 202 rooms central to the new luxury axis of BKC/Lower Parel. Pick this if your Mumbai trip leans nightlife, fashion week, or business over Gateway tourism.

name: Abode Bombay
why_special: 20-room boutique inside a restored 1910 colonial house above Colaba Causeway — design-led, art-deco-furniture, walk to Gateway/Taj/Leopold Cafe. Mumbai's first true boutique hotel and still the most distinctive small property in South Mumbai.

name: Zostel Mumbai
why_special: India's flagship backpacker chain in Andheri West — dorms ₹600–1,200, private rooms ₹1,800+. 15 min to BOM airport, walking-distance to Andheri station for South-Mumbai trips by Metro Line 1. The most reliable budget social bed in the city.
